description: Sepsis / Septic Shock population — one to two sepsis episodes per patient, predominantly inpatient and ED encounters. Clinical context: Sepsis-3 requires life-threatening organ dysfunction from infection. Septic shock is a subset with vasopressor requirement + lactate >2 mmol/L. This population is modeled as patients who experienced acute sepsis episodes over a 24-month window, with rare post-discharge outpatient follow-up. Not every patient has ICU-level illness — lab derangements vary from moderate (uncomplicated sepsis) to severe (septic shock).
do_not_flag: Systolic BP 60-89 mmHg in septic shock patients — hypotension is the defining feature of septic shock
WBC 12.0-18.0 K/uL — leukocytosis is a Sepsis-3 criterion; values near the abnormal ceiling reflect realistic leukocytosis distribution
Lactate 2.1-8.0 mmol/L — elevated lactate indicates tissue hypoperfusion; the range reflects both moderate sepsis (2-4) and septic shock (4-8+)
Creatinine 1.3-4.0 mg/dL — sepsis-induced AKI is common; values up to 4.0 are realistic for acute organ dysfunction
Platelets 30-149 K/uL — DIC and thrombocytopenia are sepsis complications
CRP 11-200 mg/L and procalcitonin 0.5-50 ng/mL — markedly elevated inflammatory markers are expected in bacterial sepsis
Temperature 100.4-105°F — fever is a hallmark sepsis presentation
High inpatient encounter rate (50%) and ED rate (42%) — sepsis requires hospitalization; outpatient encounters represent only post-discharge follow-up
Vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam prescribed together — empiric dual coverage is standard Surviving Sepsis Campaign protocol
ALT/AST 57-300 U/L — hepatic injury from sepsis-induced hypoperfusion
Low outpatient encounter count (8%) — most encounters are acute; the few outpatient encounters are post-discharge follow-up, not routine primary care

required_drug_classes.rationale: Broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour is the Surviving Sepsis Campaign Hour-1 Bundle standard of care.
20-30% of sepsis patients develop septic shock requiring vasopressor support.

required_checks: VERIFY that lactate lab values appear in the population — lactate monitoring is the Sepsis-3 cornerstone. Expected mean lactate 3-5 mmol/L across the population (reflecting a mix of moderate and severe sepsis). If lactate is absent, flag HIGH.
VERIFY that at least one broad-spectrum antibiotic appears in medications. If no antibiotic at all, flag CRITICAL.
VERIFY that inpatient encounters make up 40-60% of all encounters, and ED encounters make up 30-50%. If inpatient+ED rate <70% combined, flag HIGH — this is an acute-illness population.
CHECK that WBC is elevated in at least some patients (mean >10 K/uL expected). Normal mean WBC for all patients would be implausible in sepsis.
VERIFY that procalcitonin appears in the population — it is the primary sepsis biomarker. If completely absent, flag MEDIUM.
